paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: Ablation studies between Consistency-Bi and Consistency-Uni on test set of IWSLT14 De-En task of wait-k policy.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Average Lagging (AL) on the x-axis and BLEU score on the y-axis for three different consistency methods—Consistency-CE, Consistency-Uni, and Consistency-Bi—evaluated on the test set of the IWSLT14 De-En task under the wait-k policy. The x-axis, labeled “Average Lagging (AL),” spans from approximately 1 to 9 with tick marks at integer intervals, and is linearly scaled. The y-axis, labeled “BLEU,” ranges from 20 to 32 with major tick marks every 2 units, also linearly scaled. The purple dashed line with circular markers, representing Consistency-CE, starts at AL ≈ 1 with a BLEU score of 19, then rises sharply to BLEU ≈ 26 at AL = 3, and continues increasing more gradually to BLEU ≈ 31.5 at AL = 8.5. The green solid line with square markers, representing Consistency-Uni, begins at AL = 2 with BLEU ≈ 25.5, rises to BLEU ≈ 28 at AL = 4, then to BLEU ≈ 30.5 at AL = 6, and reaches BLEU ≈ 32.5 at AL = 8.5. The red solid line with star markers, representing Consistency-Bi, starts at AL = 2 with BLEU ≈ 26, increases to BLEU ≈ 28.5 at AL = 4, then to BLEU ≈ 30.5 at AL = 6, and peaks at BLEU ≈ 32.5 at AL = 8.5. All three lines show a generally increasing trend in BLEU as AL increases, with Consistency-Uni and Consistency-Bi closely tracking each other and consistently outperforming Consistency-CE across the range.
